liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the opening acoustic Iko Iko very sweet; The acoustic Iko Iko impressed the reviewer [18][20]
- **Ripple** (2 reviews): Reviewer suggests this may be the Ripple used on the Reckoning album; Reviewer finds it smoother and slightly shorter than the officially released live version [15][18]
- **It Must Have Been the Roses** (1 other source): Multiple mixes of this song were made for the Reckoning album on February 20, 1981 [9]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer, usually lukewarm on this song, finds this version extremely good and emotional [13]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Singled out as a hot performance [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Begins with an aborted start, which the reviewer found hilarious and had not heard before [15]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The jam meltdown after He's Gone is especially far out [14]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Reviewer found the closing Brokedown Palace gave them chills [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-26.mtx.seamons.101967.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 187 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd80-10-26.sbd.hinko.18862.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 183 min; rated 4.4/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard opens with the audience mic still on during Iko Iko, which the reviewer found charming; After the audience mic is turned off, the soundboard sounds like the Reckoning album [18][20]
- **gd80-10-26sbd.remaster.18896.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 183 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording at the start is loud, then switches to a superior-quality board source [15]
- **gd80-10-26.sony-ecm.fishman.11837.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 181 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds great but resembles an audience tape already on the archive [19]

## Around the show

- Relaxed banter during the acoustic set as the band works out what to play next [11]
- Just before Estimated Prophet, Bobby addresses the crowd in a faux Mexican accent to explain an equipment problem [14]
- This night's show is shorter than the following night's but has some great stretches [11]
- Contains a lot of jamming by late-1980 standards [14]
- One of the few standout-sounding electric shows from Radio City Music Hall [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-26.mtx.seamons.101967.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN>AIFF>Final Cut>WAV>FLAC) [1]
- **gd80-10-26.sbd.hinko.18862.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd80-10-26sbd.remaster.18896.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd80-10-26.sony-ecm.fishman.11837.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM 270 Condensors > Cassette [6]
